title.narrative: Institutional assessment Africa Regional Integration and Trade

description.narrative:
The objective of the consultancy assignment is to provide technical support to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs/Learning in identifying and developing two projects which will support actions for increased trade and regional economic integration in Africa; the consultancy will assist in preparing the necessary project documentation for the suggested interventions in line with the Danida Aid Management Guidelines.
The working hypothesis is that the support will be provided to East African Community (EAC) and Economic Committeion of West African States (ECOWAS) to strengthen their capacities and efforts to perform their roles in promoting inclusive and sustainable trade and economic integration in the East and West African regions respectively. To support MFA in drafting the Project Documents(PD) the consultants will: 1. Follow the AMG in describing the context and justification for the usage of funds allocated, outline key principles and financing modalities; theory of change and results framework, budgets and how the instrument interacts with and complements other financial support from member states and donors. The aim is to support the chosen competent authorities in addressing urgent political priorities over the next 2-3 years without distorting or complicating the existing structures and procedures.
2. Scope of work The scope of work will fall under the three main areas below. The accelerated formulation process may require a light approach to some of the activities below. Scoping activities – clarifying focus and identify partners • Identify main trends, issues, and opportunities in East and West Africa for increased trade and economic integration, especially in support of inclusive and sustainable development • Conduct a rapid mapping of the institutional landscape and competent African organs for economic integration and trade in east and west Africa, as basis for informing the focus and ensuring the coherence of the support. • Present a summary overview of existing trade protocols and agreements and state of play with ongoing reforms, with focus on best opportunities for progress • Present an outline of Danish support to trade facilitation and economic integration in Africa, with focus on coherence, synergies and results and lessons to build on • Identify two African institutions as partners, including initial partner assessment in accordance with the MFA guidelines of the chosen institutions. Partner assessments and focused design of support and modalities • Assess the main relevant deliverables and value-added of the partners to the regional trade and economic integration agendas, as basis for deciding the specific focus of the support • Asses the partners’ planning frameworks, budgets and financing positions of the chosen partners, including own generated revenues from member states and external finance from donors to identify financing needs and the most effective way to structure the and channel the Danish
